name: The Doors
hook: The Los Angeles band whose keyboard player covered the bass parts on stage, and who played on Weird Al's Doors pastiche forty years later.

blurb.age13: The Doors formed in Los Angeles in 1965: Jim Morrison singing, Ray Manzarek on keyboards, Robby Krieger on guitar and John Densmore on drums. On stage they had no bass player; Manzarek played the bass lines on a keyboard. 'Light My Fire' (1967) went to number one. Morrison was arrested after a concert in Miami in 1969 and convicted, and he died in Paris in 1971, aged 27. The band ended in 1973.
blurb.adult: Formed in Los Angeles in 1965 and signed to Elektra in 1966, the Doors blended psychedelic, blues and acid rock, with Manzarek covering the bass on keyboard bass live. 'Light My Fire' was Elektra's first Hot 100 number one. After a concert in Miami on 1 March 1969, Morrison was arrested, convicted and sentenced to six months with hard labour and a $500 fine; he was pardoned posthumously in 2010. He died in Paris on 3 July 1971; the others made two more albums and split in 1973. The RIAA counts 36 million US album sales.
